text:
Colorado won 6-1, and the scoreboard flatters them a little. The Avalanche generated 3.59 expected goals to St. Louis's 1.97, which is a clear edge in chance quality but not a rout, and the simulated replays give Colorado a 76 percent chance of winning. The gap was bigger in the finishing. Jordan Binnington faced chances worth 3.59 goals and allowed six, 2.41 more than expected, while Mackenzie Blackwood stopped all but one of 26 shots and saved about one goal more than the average goalie would have.

The game turned in the first period, when Colorado built a 1.53 to 0.43 edge in expected goals. Cale Makar opened the scoring at 4:09 and Martin Necas doubled it at 13:12, both at even strength. The second period was closer on chance quality (0.96 to 0.50), yet Colorado scored four times. Josh Manson's snap shot at 5:38 carried only a 2 percent chance of going in, and Artturi Lehkonen made it 4-0 at 11:40. Nicolas Roy and Necas then scored 23 seconds apart late in the period to make it 6-0.

St. Louis played its best hockey after that, out-chancing Colorado 1.04 to 1.10 in the third and nearly matching them. Dalibor Dvorsky's backhand at 2:34 broke the shutout. Necas finished with two goals and an assist, Nathan MacKinnon had three assists, and neither team scored on the power play (0 for 2 for St. Louis, 0 for 4 for Colorado).
